summary: Adds EQL v3 support: a new typed schema (`@cipherstash/stack/eql/v3`, `/v3`), an `encryptedSupabaseV3` adapter, `eqlVersion` wire selection on the client (protect-ffi 0.26 -> 0.27 for everyone), and a CLI v3 install/upgrade path with two vendored ~36k-line SQL bundles. The v2 code is refactored into overridable seams that are meant to keep v2 behaviour unchanged. The most material risk is in the CLI: unlike the v2 bundle, which keeps the customer column type `public.eql_v2_encrypted` outside the dropped schema, the v3 bundle defines every customer column domain inside `eql_v3` and opens with `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE`. The new `stash eql upgrade --eql-version 3` and `install --eql-version 3 --force` both run that bundle, so on a database that already has v3-typed columns they would drop those columns and their encrypted data. Nothing guards against this and no test covers it. Secondary risks: the v3 Supabase filters send full ciphertext envelopes in GET query strings (documented as interim), the free-text `like`/`ilike` defaults silently miss matches, and the FFI bump for v2 users could not be verified here. No tests were run; CI results were not provided.

behaviour_changes.description: New CLI flag `--eql-version <2|3>` on `stash eql install` and `stash eql upgrade`. With 3, the installer runs the vendored v3 bundle (full, or the Supabase variant with operator classes removed) in a transaction and, for Supabase, grants on `eql_v3` and `eql_v3_internal`. The bundle starts with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE and eql_v3_internal CASCADE, and the customer column domains (e.g. eql_v3.text_search) live in eql_v3.

v3 `isInstalled` needs both eql_v3 and eql_v3_internal. A database that has only eql_v3 (an older pre-alpha.2 generation) counts as not installed, so a plain `stash eql install --eql-version 3` reruns the dropping bundle over it.

New public entry points `@cipherstash/stack/eql/v3` and `@cipherstash/stack/v3` (ESM+CJS+types) and `encryptedSupabaseV3`. EncryptionClient methods widen from EncryptedTable/JsPlaintext to structural BuildableTable/Plaintext (adds Date). `Encryption()` now throws when v2 and v3 tables are mixed, and passes the resolved `eqlVersion` to protect-ffi `newClient`. This stays `undefined` for v2-only schema sets.
@cipherstash/protect-ffi goes from 0.26.0 to 0.27.0 for every @cipherstash/stack consumer (native per-platform binaries and the wasm-inline entry), including v2-only users.

The v3 Supabase builder encrypts each filter operand with `encrypt()` (a full storage envelope: ciphertext plus all index terms), not with `encryptQuery`, and sends it as JSON text in the PostgREST filter value, which travels in GET query strings.

v3 Supabase `like`/`ilike` (and `not`/`or` variants) on encrypted columns become PostgREST `cs` (bloom-filter containment). The default match options keep `include_original: true`, which per the code's own comment stops substring patterns from matching.

The v2 Supabase builder, encryption operations and model helpers are refactored: private members become protected, there are new dialect hook methods, column-name mapping (identity for v2), and `assertValidNumericValue` is now also applied on the lock-context encrypt path. `encryptQuery(array, opts)` now takes the single-value path instead of batch mode when opts are given. The bigint case is removed from `inferQueryOpFromPlaintext`. `resolveLockContext` adds a structural `identityContext` check.

CI gains a type-test step and a check that the vendored v3 SQL bundles match the fixture. A new FTA complexity workflow is added. Shipped CLI dist now includes the v3 SQL files (copied from src/sql) and the updated stash-supabase skill.

failure_scenarios.title: `stash eql upgrade --eql-version 3` (or install --force) drops customer columns typed with eql_v3 domains
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user with tables already using eql_v3.* columns (as the docs instruct) runs `stash eql upgrade --eql-version 3`, runs `stash eql install --eql-version 3 --force`, or runs a plain v3 install against an older-generation v3 install (eql_v3 present, eql_v3_internal absent).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: upgradeCommand checks isInstalled({eqlVersion:3}) and then calls installer.install({eqlVersion:3}) (upgrade.ts:53,96). install() runs the bundled SQL and then COMMITs (installer/index.ts:335,341). The v3 bundle opens with `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE` (cipherstash-encrypt-v3.sql:38), and the column domains are defined in that schema (e.g. CREATE DOMAIN eql_v3.timestamp, :545). In PostgreSQL, dropping a domain with CASCADE drops the table columns of that type. The v2 bundle avoids exactly this: it creates the customer column type in `public` and only if absent, with the note 'Customer data columns use this type, so it must not be dropped' (cipherstash-encrypt.sql:28-41). The test helper for this change even notes the bundle 'must never run unconditionally' against a shared database (helpers/eql-v3.ts:80-82), but the CLI upgrade path runs it unconditionally once v3 is detected. BC-2 makes this reachable without --force for older-generation installs.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every eql_v3-typed column in the database is silently removed in a committed transaction. The encrypted data in those columns is lost and can only come back from a backup. The CLI reports success ('EQL extensions upgraded').

existing_verification.description: installer.test.ts checks that the v3 bundle and grants are issued and that isInstalled requires both schemas (mocked pg). It does not check behaviour against existing v3 columns.

missing_verification: Integration test: create a table with eql_v3.text_search columns and data, run `stash eql upgrade --eql-version 3`, and assert the columns and rows survive (or that the CLI refuses).
Confirmation from the EQL maintainers of whether the v3 bundle is meant to be re-runnable over live data.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Until the bundle is non-destructive, make v3 upgrade, --force and stale-generation reinstall refuse (or require an explicit destructive confirmation) when any column in pg_attribute depends on a type in eql_v3. Alternatively, move the column domains out of the dropped schema, as v2 does with public.eql_v2_encrypted. Document clearly that v3 alpha upgrades are destructive.

failure_scenarios.title: v3 Supabase filters put full ciphertext envelopes and all index terms in GET URLs
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any v3 Supabase filter (`eq`, `gt`, `like`, `in`, `or`, ...) on an encrypted column issued through PostgREST.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: encryptCollectedTerms calls `encryptionClient.encrypt()` per operand and returns JSON.stringify of the full storage payload (query-builder-v3.ts:194-249). The code and docs say this carries a decryptable `c` plus every index term (hm, ob/ORE, bloom) and lands in URL logs (supabase-sdk.md:158-168).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Ciphertexts and searchable index terms (including order-revealing terms) are kept in proxy, CDN and Supabase request logs outside the database's access controls. This widens what an attacker with log access can analyse; plaintext is still not exposed without keys. Large envelopes, or `.in()` with many values, can also exceed URL length limits (a loud failure).

existing_verification.description: supabase-v3-builder.test.ts checks operator mapping and encoding with a mocked Supabase client. It does not check log or URL exposure.

missing_verification: A security sign-off that the interim full-envelope operand (tracked as CIP-3402 in comments) is acceptable to release, and a measurement of operand URL size per domain.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Gate encryptedSupabaseV3 as experimental/alpha in release notes. Send filters via POST/RPC where possible. Ship the term-only query envelope before GA.

failure_scenarios.title: v3 `like`/`ilike` silently return no or partial rows with default match options or `%` patterns
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user declares `types.TextSearch(...)` without `freeTextSearch({ include_original: false })`, or passes a v2-style `%alice%` pattern (as the v2 sections of the same skill show), and queries with `.like`/`.ilike` through encryptedSupabaseV3.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Encrypted like/ilike become `cs` on the bloom filter (query-builder-v3.ts:260-277). The operand is a full envelope whose bloom includes the original whole value when include_original is true, the default in defaultMatchOpts (match-defaults.ts:33-41). The code comment says such patterns then only match exact values (query-builder-v3.ts:72-78).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Search features return empty or incomplete results without an error. This is functional degradation, not data loss.

existing_verification.description: Builder unit test only checks that like/ilike become `cs`. Whether the result is correct depends on the live-gated pg/Supabase tests, which were not run.

missing_verification: Live test that substring `.ilike` finds rows with the default TextSearch configuration (expected to fail today) and with include_original:false.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Default include_original to false for v3 domains used through Supabase, or reject/warn on `%` and on include_original:true at query time.

failure_scenarios.title: protect-ffi 0.27 bump changes v2 behaviour for existing users
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any existing v2 user upgrades @cipherstash/stack and gets protect-ffi 0.27.0 (native or WASM).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The dependency moves to 0.27.0 (package.json:247), and newClient now receives an `eqlVersion` key (undefined for v2) (encryption/index.ts:153-167). The comments claim v2 output stays byte-identical, but that is a property of the FFI release and cannot be checked in this checkout (no node_modules, no network).
failure_scenarios.consequence: If 0.27 changes v2 payload shape, query-term encoding or error codes, v2 users could write payloads that older readers or the installed eql_v2 SQL handle differently. That is a cross-version data-compatibility problem.

existing_verification.description: Existing v2 suites (encrypt-query*.test.ts, supabase.test.ts) exercise the FFI, but most are gated on live credentials.

missing_verification: A CI run of the live v2 suites against 0.27.0, and a golden-payload comparison of v2 encrypt/encryptQuery output between 0.26 and 0.27.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Confirm that the protect-ffi 0.27 changelog states v2 wire output is unchanged, and run the credentialed v2 suites before release.

recommended_controls.description: Add a pre-flight guard to `eql upgrade --eql-version 3`, `install --eql-version 3 --force` and the stale-generation reinstall: query for user columns whose type lives in eql_v3 and abort (or require an explicit destructive flag) if any exist.
Add a Postgres integration test that seeds an eql_v3.text_search column with rows, runs the v3 upgrade, and asserts the data survives or the command refuses.

State in the changeset, CLI help and the stash-supabase skill that v3 is alpha and that rerunning the v3 bundle is destructive. Mark encryptedSupabaseV3 as experimental and flag the URL-logged operands.
Have the EQL/security owners sign off on the interim full-envelope filter operand and the include_original default for v3 free-text search.
Run the credentialed v2 suites and a 0.26 vs 0.27 golden-payload comparison before publishing.

evidence.claim: upgradeCommand checks isInstalled({eqlVersion}) and then calls installer.install({... eqlVersion}) with no check for existing data.
The v3 bundle runs DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE and DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3_internal CASCADE.
Customer column domains (eql_v3.timestamp, eql_v3.timestamp_eq, ...) are created inside the eql_v3 schema.
install() rejects --latest for v3, loads the bundled v3 SQL, runs it, and COMMITs.
v3 isInstalled needs both eql_v3 and eql_v3_internal. The comment says a stale install is treated as not installed so the bundle replaces it by dropping both schemas.
Filter operands are produced by encrypt() (full storage envelope) and JSON-stringified as the PostgREST filter value.
Encrypted like/ilike become `cs`. With the default include_original:true, substring patterns only match when the pattern equals the stored value.
resolveEqlVersion throws on mixed v2/v3 schemas, returns undefined for v2-only and 3 for v3-only. The result is passed to newClient as eqlVersion.
New exports ./eql/v3 and ./v3 (import/require/types). tsup entries were added for src/eql/v3/index.ts and src/encryption/v3.ts.
@cipherstash/protect-ffi dependency is 0.27.0 (was 0.26.0). The lockfile updates all per-platform binaries.
defaultMatchOpts returns include_original: true, shared by the v2 freeTextSearch and the v3 domain builders.
The docs acknowledge that full-envelope operands carry a decryptable ciphertext plus all index terms in GET query strings, which can land in URL logs.
The v2 builder is refactored to protected members with dialect hooks whose defaults are identity / v2 behaviour.
CLI build copies src/sql (now including the v3 bundles) into dist/sql.
CLI build copies the repo skills directory into dist/skills for `stash init` to put into customer repos.
The docs instruct users to create tables with columns typed eql_v3.text_search, eql_v3.integer_ord and eql_v3.timestamp_ord.
By contrast, the v2 bundle creates public.eql_v2_encrypted only if absent, outside the dropped schema, because customer columns use it.
v3 installer tests check the bundle and grants and the two-schema isInstalled with a mocked pg client. No test covers existing v3 columns.
The v2 Supabase integration suite is skipped unless SUPABASE_ENABLED.
